speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, I'm Connie Loizis.
zh: 嗨,我是 Connie Loizis。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is Alex Gove.
zh: 这位是 Alex Gove。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is Strictly VC Download.
zh: 这里是 Strictly VC Download。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hello, and welcome back to Strictly VC Download.
zh: 大家好,欢迎回到 Strictly VC Download。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, Alex and I are joined by former Vice President Al Gore and Lila Preston, Co-Head of Growth Equity at Generation Investment Management.
zh: 今天,我和 Alex 请到了前副总统 Al Gore 以及 Generation Investment Management 增长股权联席主管 Lila Preston。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this conversation, we get into the massive energy demands of AI and data centers.
zh: 在这期对话中,我们深入探讨了 AI 和数据中心的巨大能源需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why Gore thinks the backlash deserves concern but not panic, and where he and Preston see some of the biggest opportunities for investors and founders as the energy transition accelerates even faster than Gore imagined it would, due largely to some unhappy world events, including the war in Ukraine and the fight over the Strait of Hormuz as part of the U.S. war with Iran.
zh: 为什么 Gore 认为反对浪潮值得担忧但不必恐慌,以及随着能源转型的加速甚至超过 Gore 当初的想象——这主要由于一些令人不快的世界事件,包括乌克兰战争,以及作为美国与伊朗战争一部分的霍尔木兹海峡之争——他和 Preston 看到了投资者和创始人的哪些最大机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: We relatedly talk about the surprising pace of solar adoption, the challenges facing nuclear power, and why advances in AI could ultimately help make industries from agriculture to energy far more efficient, even as those data centers needed to support it face growing opposition.
zh: 我们相应地谈到了太阳能普及的惊人速度、核能面临的挑战,以及为什么 AI 的进步最终可能帮助从农业到能源等各行各业变得更高效,即使支持它所需的数据中心正面临日益增长的反対。

speaker: Unknown
en: This has become something of an annual chat with Gore and Preston, one we always enjoy.
zh: 与 Gore 和 Preston 的对谈某种程度上已成了一年一度的节目,我们总是很享受。

speaker: Unknown
en: We hope you enjoy hearing from them too, and we will see you back here next week.
zh: 我们希望你们也喜欢听他们的分享,我们下周再见。

speaker: Unknown
en: Guys, thank you so much.
zh: 各位,非常感谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know it's a busy week for you, Lila.
zh: 我知道这周你们很忙,Lila。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were just talking about how crazy your schedules are.
zh: 我们刚才还在聊你们的日程有多疯狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thank you both so much for making time for us.
zh: 所以非常感谢你们两位抽时间给我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love your report.
zh: 我很喜欢你们的报告。

speaker: Unknown
en: Always fascinating to read through.
zh: 读起来总是很引人入胜。

speaker: Unknown
en: This one certainly sounds, I don't know, more optimistic even than in recent years.
zh: 这一份听起来,怎么说呢,甚至比近几年的更加乐观。

speaker: Unknown
en: But Mr. Gore, I wanted to start with the headlines first, which of course is
zh: 但是 Gore 先生,我想先从新闻头条开始,那当然就是

speaker: Unknown
en: AI and data centers.
zh: AI 和数据中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: So much focus on this right now.
zh: 现在对这个的关注太多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have called the data center backlash a cause for deep concern, but not panic.
zh: 你曾把对数据中心的反对称为一个值得深切关注但不值得恐慌的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: That the strain on land and water and grids is real, but also that the build out is probably inevitable.
zh: 对土地、水和电网的压力是真实存在的,但这轮建设也几乎是不可避免的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this fight should really be about forcing data centers to pair with
zh: 所以这场斗争实际上应该是迫使数据中心与

speaker: Unknown
en: Renewable power rather than trying to just stop construction outright.
zh: 可再生能源配套,而不是试图彻底阻止建设。

speaker: Unknown
en: This fight is getting much bigger and escalating really quickly.
zh: 这场斗争正变得规模大得多,而且升级得非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you make of what's happening out there?
zh: 你怎么看待外面正在发生的事情?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, the list of concerns where advanced AI is concerned is a long list.
zh: 嗯,就先进 AI 而言,值得担忧的事项是一长串。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the comments that I've made about energy use
zh: 我关于能源使用

speaker: Unknown
en: And emissions from AI data centers is really focused on that concern.
zh: 和 AI 数据中心排放所发表的评论,正是聚焦于这一担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I do think it's not a cause for panic where the emissions are concerned.
zh: 我确实认为,就排放而言,这不是一个值得恐慌的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is a matter of deep concern that some of the hyperscalers are jumping into new methane turbines.
zh: 一些超大规模云厂商正在跳入新的甲烷涡轮机,这是令人深切担忧的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I much prefer those who are...
zh: 而我更倾向于那些

speaker: Unknown
en: Supplying their energy needs with renewables and batteries.
zh: 用可再生能源和电池来满足其能源需求的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's going to be a continued shift in that direction for a lot of reasons, not least because they're more competitive when they get the cheapest sources of electricity.
zh: 我认为这个方向上的转变会持续下去,原因有很多,尤其是因为当他们获得最便宜的电力来源时,可再生能源更具竞争力。

speaker: Unknown
en: But of course, there are other concerns related to advanced AI that have been much in the news just in the last few days.
zh: 但当然,还有与先进 AI 相关的其他担忧,就在最近几天成为了新闻焦点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I do think that regulating
zh: 我确实认为,监管

speaker: Unknown
en: The frontier models is one of the two issues most appropriate for a renewed cooperation between the US and China.
zh: 前沿模型是美中重续合作最合适的两大议题之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just in the last few days, one high official in China expressed concern about
zh: 就在最近几天,中国的一位高级官员表达了对

speaker: Unknown
en: The implications of advanced AI for the Communist Party's continued dominance of that country.
zh: 先进 AI 对该党继续主导那个国家的影响的担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And other than Donald Trump, most everybody else in the US is concerned about some of the risks that people inside the industry have raised, both at Anthropic and OpenAI and Elon Musk joined in as well.
zh: 而除了 Donald Trump 之外,美国几乎所有人都对业内人士提出的某些风险感到担忧,包括 Anthropic、OpenAI 内部的人,Elon Musk 也加入了这一行列。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that
zh: 我认为,

speaker: Unknown
en: It's unfortunate that Donald Trump is probably not going to be able to reawaken U.S.-China cooperation.
zh: Donald Trump 大概率无法重振美中合作,这很不幸。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope I'm proven wrong about that.
zh: 我希望我被证明是错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think the agenda for the years ahead is very clear.
zh: 但我认为,未来几年的议程是非常清晰的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that the elections coming up in November will also contribute to that shift.
zh: 而且我认为,11 月即将到来的选举也将推动这一转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, overall, the increased electricity production from renewable energy plus batteries now matches and even exceeds the increase in global energy use.
zh: 但是,你知道,总体而言,可再生能源加电池带来的电力产量的增长,现在已经赶上甚至超过了全球能源使用的增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are seeing the momentum continue to build, and we're seeing the beginnings of displacement of fossil fuels by renewable energy, even as overall energy use increases.
zh: 我们看到这一势头继续增强,我们看到可再生能源开始取代化石燃料,即使整体能源使用在增加。

speaker: Unknown
en: One reason, as this year's sustainability trends report,
zh: 正如今年的可持续发展趋势报告

speaker: Unknown
en: Highlights is that the interruption of oil and gas supplies from the Persian Gulf and now, of course, the Red Sea route is threatened also.
zh: 所强调的一个原因是,来自波斯湾的石油和天然气供应中断,而现在,红海航线当然也受到了威胁。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the second time in four years that the world has been brutally reminded
zh: 这是四年来世界第二次被残酷地提醒

speaker: Unknown
en: That fossil fuels are a very difficult and unreliable source of energy.
zh: 化石燃料是一种非常困难且不可靠的能源来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: Price volatility has increased dramatically.
zh: 价格波动性急剧上升。

speaker: Unknown
en: The cutoff of supplies, again, the second time in four years.
zh: 供应中断,这已经是四年内的第二次了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This has caused a break in the previous pattern.
zh: 这打破了以往的模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: The president of South Korea
zh: 韩国总统

speaker: Unknown
en: said just recently, this shows us we can no longer put off the transition away from fossil fuels.
zh: 最近说过,这告诉我们,我们不能再拖延从化石燃料的转型了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just a few days ago, the leadership in Thailand made a dramatic announcement that they're switching from LNG to solar.
zh: 就在几天前,泰国领导层做出了一个引人注目的宣布,他们将从液化天然气转向太阳能。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've seen the surge in solar panel sales with reports that now were hidden from the public
zh: 我们看到太阳能电池板销量激增,而相关报告此前一直被向公众隐瞒

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, the common dowry in Pakistan and parts of Pakistan is now three panels and an inverter.
zh: 如今,在巴基斯坦及巴基斯坦部分地区,常见的嫁妆已经是三块太阳能板加一台逆变器。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think we're at a real turning point.
zh: 所以我认为我们正处在一个真正的转折点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Getting back to the U.S. for a second, we have not embraced solar and wind, at least in recent years, and it seems that integrating these power sources into the grid is also becoming a real issue.
zh: 回到美国的话题,我们近年来没有拥抱太阳能和风能,而把这些电源整合进电网似乎也正在成为一个真正的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do we need to do to improve our grid in the way that we can accept these power sources?
zh: 我们需要做什么来改进我们的电网,使其能够接纳这些电源?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, as this year's STR points out, the electrical grids around the world are the principal limiting factor of this transition now.
zh: 嗯,正如今年的 STR 所指出的,世界各地的电网现在是这场转型的主要限制因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's worth remembering the only technology that's come down in price faster than solar electricity is utility scale batteries.
zh: 但值得记住的是,唯一一个价格下降速度比太阳能电力更快的技术,就是电网级规模的电池。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they are now being dotted around many of the grids, even as other improvements are also easing the task
zh: 如今它们正被散布部署在许多电网中,即使其他改进也在减轻这项任务

speaker: Unknown
en: I think of upgrading the grids, but it remains a serious challenge for sure.
zh: 我想到的是电网升级,但这无疑仍然是一个严峻的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was just going to add, Alex, that I believe that the move from the supply being the challenge to the grid resilience being a challenge, we recognize that in the report.
zh: Alex,我正想补充一点,我相信从供应是挑战转变为电网韧性是挑战,我们在报告中认识到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we talk a lot about the imperative of grid flexibility, interconnection, and the now optimization of the mix because it's increasingly diverse.
zh: 我们大量讨论了电网灵活性、互联互通的紧迫性,以及如今对能源结构的优化,因为它正变得越来越多元化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is actually linked to the imperative to move to more renewables, but also secure, durable power sources.
zh: 这实际上与转向更多可再生能源的紧迫性相关,同时也关系到安全、持久的电源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's been a core focus of ours also from the investment side.
zh: 这也是我们从投资角度的一个核心关注点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And fossil fuels are becoming an intermittent source of energy for many
zh: 而化石燃料正在成为许多人眼中一种间歇性的能源来源

speaker: Unknown
en: So heavily on exports from the Persian Gulf.
zh: 高度依赖波斯湾的出口。

speaker: Unknown
en: And unfortunately, in too many countries, nuclear is becoming somewhat intermittent as the rivers become too hot and the water levels drop too low.
zh: 而且不幸的是,在太多国家,核电也正变得有点间歇性,因为河水温度过高、水位过低。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the reliability of solar and wind and batteries
zh: 因此,太阳能、风能和电池的可靠性

speaker: Unknown
en: It guarantees that their share of the production of electricity will continue to increase.
zh: 保证了它们在电力生产中的份额将持续增加。

speaker: Unknown
en: 86% of all new electricity production worldwide last year was renewables.
zh: 去年全球所有新增电力生产中有 86% 是可再生能源。

speaker: Unknown
en: 91% in the U.S. in spite of Donald Trump's best efforts to slow it down.
zh: 在美国这一比例是 91%,尽管 Donald Trump 尽了最大努力去拖慢它。

speaker: Unknown
en: You mentioned nuclear.
zh: 你提到了核能。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's tremendous venture enthusiasm around small nuclear reactors and newer nuclear technologies.
zh: 围绕小型核反应堆和较新的核技术,存在着巨大的风投热情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you see this as a real investable opportunity or do the timelines and the regulation and the capital requirements make nuclear particularly difficult?
zh: 你认为这是一个真正可投资的机会,还是说时间线、监管和资本需求使核能变得特别困难?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, some of the safety engineering required for nuclear doesn't scale down in cost as the output of electricity scales down.
zh: 嗯,核能所需的某些安全工程,并不会随着发电规模的缩小而相应降低成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you may have noticed that some short sellers made a windfall betting against these small modular reactors just a couple of months ago.
zh: 你可能注意到,就在几个月前,一些做空者靠押注做空这些小型模块化反应堆赚了一笔横财。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hal Harvey, one of the leading energy experts, has famously said that the new modular reactors are quite amazing.
zh: Hal Harvey,能源领域顶尖专家之一,曾有一句名言:新的模块化反应堆相当了不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're smaller, safer, cheaper, and don't exist.
zh: 它们更小、更安全、更便宜,而且不存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I hope they will exist.
zh: 而且我希望它们会存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm optimistic
zh: 我是乐观的

speaker: Unknown
en: It's still quite a long ways out.
zh: 但仍然还有相当长的一段路。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the early pilots have been disappointing.
zh: 而且早期的试点项目一直令人失望。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why the short sellers have bet against them successfully.
zh: 这就是做空者们成功押注做空它们的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I recently visited Oak Ridge, Tennessee, where nuclear energy began.
zh: 但我最近访问了田纳西州的 Oak Ridge,核能就是在那里起步的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are a hundred different designs.
zh: 那里有上百种不同的设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're always to play a significant role at any time very soon.
zh: 它们总是想要在短期内扮演重要角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, I hope they will develop them safely and profitably, but it's quite a ways off in my opinion.
zh: 再说一次,我希望它们能被安全且有利可图地开发出来,但在我看来还有相当长的路要走。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your report says clean energy investment has reached $2.2 trillion annually, but needs to roughly double to $4.5 trillion by the early 2030s.
zh: 你的报告说清洁能源投资已达到每年 2.2 万亿美元,但需要在 2030 年代初之前大致翻倍至 4.5 万亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where are the biggest investable gaps today?
zh: 今天最大的可投资缺口在哪里?

speaker: Unknown
en: Areas where technology is ready, but the capital still isn't showing up?
zh: 那些技术已经就绪、但资本仍未到位的领域?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, if you look at the global market, there is now twice as much investment in clean energy as in fossil fuel energy.
zh: 嗯,如果你看全球市场,现在清洁能源的投资已经是化石能源投资的两倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: I expect those trends to continue, but I think that this transition is inevitable.
zh: 我预计这些趋势会持续下去,但我认为这场转型是不可避免的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The remaining question is whether we will accomplish the transition in time to avoid some of the negative tip
zh: 剩下的问题是,我们是否能及时完成这场转型,以避免一些负面临界点

speaker: Unknown
en: Gulfstream, part of the Atlantic meridonal overturning current, like the loss of the warm water coral reef systems, like the transition of the Amazon from a rainforest to a savanna, there are unfortunately eight or nine other major negative tipping points.
zh: 比如大西洋经向翻转环流中的湾流,比如温水珊瑚礁系统的消失,比如亚马逊从雨林向稀树草原的转变——不幸的是,还有八九个其他重大的负面临界点。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, there's been a lot of focus on the grid.
zh: 你知道，人们一直非常关注电网。

speaker: Unknown
en: So both the supply of energy and now grid resilience, as I mentioned, but there's equally massive industries that need to be redesigned.
zh: 所以既有能源供应，还有我刚才提到的电网韧性，但也有同样庞大的行业需要被重新设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, we have the benefits of now AI in the mix to potentially do this, but think about, you know, transportation, you know, EVs have been up and one in four of the global automotive fleet is an electric vehicle.
zh: 再说一次，我们现在拥有 AI 参与其中的优势来潜在地实现这一点，但想想看，你知道，交通领域，你知道，电动车一直在上升，全球汽车保有量的四分之一是电动车。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a really good indicator,
zh: 这是一个非常好的指标,

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are new sales.
zh: 这些是新增销售。

speaker: Unknown
en: New sales.
zh: 新增销售。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, exactly.
zh: 是的，正是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: And despite in the U.S. it's maybe slower globally, this is a trend that's taking off.
zh: 尽管在美国可能慢一些，但在全球范围内，这是一个正在起飞的趋势。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now think about all of the infrastructure that's needed around the EV.
zh: 但现在想想围绕电动车所需要的所有基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's charging, it's battery optimization, it's the software that does preventative maintenance.
zh: 它是充电，它是电池优化，它是做预防性维护的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like there's a whole swath of requirements, especially as autonomy meets EVs and thinking about simulation software and physical world AI.
zh: 比如有一整片需求，尤其是当自动驾驶遇上电动车时，还要考虑仿真软件和物理世界 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about those pockets of the economy that definitely could benefit from investment.
zh: 想想经济中那些肯定能从投资中受益的角落。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other area within the report I'll cite is around agriculture.
zh: 我要引用的报告中另一个领域是关于农业的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, we saw with the Strait of Hormuz closure the fact that with 30 percent of nitrogen supply passing through the straits, there was a spike of over 50 percent in the short term after that of nitrogen prices.
zh: 而且，你知道，我们从霍尔木兹海峡关闭事件中看到，由于全球 30% 的氮供应经过该海峡，此后短期内氮价格上涨了超过 50%。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that really hurts farmers.
zh: 而这真的伤害了农民。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where is the capital flowing to help?
zh: 资本流向了哪里来提供帮助？

speaker: Unknown
en: Farmers with resilient regenerative practices, whether it's using biology instead of chemistry, using advanced robotics, using data sets and computer science to drive yield improvements.
zh: 帮助农民采用有韧性的再生实践，无论是用生物学替代化学，使用先进机器人，使用数据集和计算机科学来推动产量提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like these are massive investment opportunities that we see related to these trends.
zh: 比如这些是我们看到的与这些趋势相关的大量投资机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: You mentioned in the report that your firm is invested in a synthetic fertilizer company.
zh: 你在报告中提到，你们公司投资了一家合成肥料公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Could you elaborate on that?
zh: 你能详细谈谈吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually a company using biology to replace chemistry in agriculture.
zh: 它实际上是一家用生物学替代农业中化学的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a company called Pivot Bio, and it's an example of not relying on fossil feedstocks for the production of nitrogen for growers.
zh: 它是一家叫 Pivot Bio 的公司，它是一个不让种植者的氮肥生产依赖化石原料的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's interesting about that is certainly that it is using a fraction of global resources, energy required, as well as production
zh: 关于这一点有趣的是，它当然只使用了全球资源的一小部分、所需能源，以及生产

speaker: Unknown
